function: Beamforming inference: a conditional WGAN-GP generates the full high-dimensional beamforming matrix from the low-dimensional matrix computed with WMMSE on channel information of a few antennas (pp. 2-3).
system: Downlink mmWave 60 GHz, 50 MHz; full-digital BS, 32 RF chains, antenna sets of 8 and 32; 4 single-antenna users; spacing 0.5 or 0.1 lambda; no RIS (pp. 2, 4).
method: Conditional WGAN-GP (encoder-decoder generator with skip connections, convolutional discriminator), Wasserstein plus L2 loss, supervised with WMMSE labels; RMSProp, 50 epochs, batch size 1; no transfer experiment (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: WAIR-D open-source dataset built on practical scenario maps, scenario 2 case 1 (10,000 users, one BS); 250 random samples split 4:1; estimation error -20 dB (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Same scenario for training and test (random 4:1 split of 250 samples); SNR 10 dB, estimation error -20 dB; antenna number 1 and spacing varied (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE (also the training target). Learned: DNN [13], self-supervised hybrid deep learning beamforming by F. Zhu et al., compared in Fig. 8 only (p. 5).
metrics: NMSE of inferred versus WMMSE beamforming matrix (Fig. 7); sum spectral efficiency versus antenna number 1 (Fig. 8); running time (Fig. 6) (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Fig. 6 runtime on CPU: over 50% less than WMMSE alone; orders O(L(Nt_high)^3) for WMMSE versus O(L(Nt_low)^3)+O(Nr(Nt_high)^2+(Nt_high)^3) proposed (pp. 4-5).
openness: none for the authors' own code; uses the public WAIR-D dataset [14], arXiv:2212.02159 (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "the recently released open-source dataset WAIR-D [14]" and "we choose scenario-2 in WAIR-D for our experiment"; a public dataset built on practical scenario maps, not one of the listed models, so flagged for the reviewer (see notes).
q2_support: p. 4: "we randomly select 250 samples from the dataset and split them into two subsets with a 4:1 ratio"; the test set is held out from the same scenario. p. 3: "transfer learning can be employed to accelerate the adaptation to the channel" is only suggested, not tested. Not met.
q3_support: p. 5: "spectral efficiency of the proposed method and the WMMSE as well as the DNN [13] method"; WMMSE is the non-learned baseline and DNN [13] is an earlier learned beamformer (ref. [13], p. 5), compared on spectral efficiency in Fig. 8.
q4_support: p. 4: "inferring high-dimensional beamforming matrices from low-dimensional ones reduces the time required by over 50%"; p. 5 also gives the complexity orders of WMMSE and of the proposed scheme.
q5_support: p. 4: "the recently released open-source dataset WAIR-D [14]" and "we choose scenario-2 in WAIR-D for our experiment"; trains and tests on this public channel dataset. No link to the authors' own code.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match the work. Table I and Figs. 6-8 were read from the page images (pp. 4-5). q1 and q5 rest on WAIR-D [14], a public channel dataset that the paper describes as built on practical scenario maps and contrasts with DeepMIMO; the paper does not itself say ray tracing, so the reviewer should confirm that it counts as another public ray-tracing dataset. Table I gives antenna number 2 = 32 whereas the text for Fig. 8 fixes it at 64. Only 250 samples are used.
